ceramic.title: Lithia Motors, Inc. (LAD) Financial Statement Analysis (2026)
ceramic.snippet:
A quick health check on Lithia Motors reveals a mixed but concerning picture. The company is profitable, with revenues of  $9.68 billion and net income of  $217.1 million in the most recent quarter. However, it is not generating real cash from its operations; operating cash flow was negative  -$98.4 million and free cash flow was negative  -$207.3 million . The balance sheet is not safe, burdened by  $14.7 billion in total debt against a mere  $206.5 million in cash. This combination of negative cash flow and high debt signals significant near-term financial stress, suggesting the company is borrowing to fund its activities, including shareholder returns.

  From the income statement, Lithia shows consistent profitability, though with some recent pressure. Annual revenue for 2024 was strong at  $36.2 billion , and recent quarterly revenues have been stable around  $9.6 billion . Gross margins have remained steady, floating between  15.3% and  15.7% over the last year, indicating stable pricing power on its vehicle sales. However, operating and net profit margins are thin, at  4.52% and  2.24% respectively in the latest quarter. While net income remains positive, it declined from  $256.1 million in the second quarter to  $217.1 million in the third. For investors, this shows Lithia can control its direct costs but struggles to translate high revenue into substantial bottom-line profit after accounting for operating expenses and interest.

  The companys reported earnings do not appear to be real in terms of cash conversion. In the last two quarters, net income totaled  $473.2 million , but operating cash flow was a combined negative  -$89.1 million . This major disconnect signals that profits are tied up in non-cash assets. The primary culprit is working capital. The cash flow statement shows a  -$478.8 million negative change in working capital in the most recent quarter, driven by factors like increases in inventory and receivables.
